in_hebrew.name: עדריאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם עדריאן מקורו בלטינית, ופירושו 'מנהיג הצאן' או 'פקיד צאן'. בברית החדשה, השם 'אדריאן' מופיע פעמיים: 'אדריאנוס' (Ἀδριανός) - בשם היהודי של האפיפיור 'אדריאנוס הראשון' (Adrian I), ו'אדריאנוס' (Ἀδριανός) - בשם הבישוף הקדוש 'אדריאנוס' (Saint Adrian).

in_greek.name: Αδριανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο όνομα Αδριανός προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη για τον κατώτερο έφορο (ἀνθύπατος), τον οποίο ορίζει ο κύριος. Ως όνομα, Αδριανός συνδέεται με την ηγεσία και τον έλεγχο. Στα NT, το όνομα Αδριανός εμφανίζεται δύο φορές: 'Αδριανός' (Ἀδριανός) - στο όνομα του 'Απωστόλου Αδριανού' (Apostle Adrian) και 'Αδριανός' (Ἀδριανός) - στο όνομα του 'Αγίου Αδριανού' (Saint Adrian).

in_latin.name: Adrianus
in_latin.meaning: dux pastorum, leader of the flocks
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Adrianus originem habet a vocabulo Latinorum, significans ducem pastoralem, ducem pastorum. In Novo Testamento, nomen Adrianus apparit semel: 'Adrianus' - in nomine Apostoli 'Adrianus' et 'Adrianus' - in nomine Sancti 'Adrianus'.

in_english.name: Adrien
in_english.meaning: leader of the flocks, herding or cattle master
in_english.long_meaning: The name Adrian is derived from the Latin name 'Adrianus', meaning 'leader of the flocks' or 'herding master'. In the New Testament, the name Adrian appears twice: 'Adrian' - in the name of the Apostle 'Adrian' and 'Adrian' - in the name of Saint 'Adrian'. The name has historically been associated with Christian saints, particularly Saint Adrian of Nicomedia, a 4th-century martyr. In modern times, the name Adrian has become popular across various Christian cultures, symbolizing leadership, courage, and devotion.

biblical_reference.note: The name Adrian is associated with two biblical figures: the Apostle Adrian and Saint Adrian of Nicomedia.

saint_reference.note: Saint Adrian was a 4th-century martyr and bishop of Nicomedia, known for his bravery and devotion to Christianity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Adrien has a rich cultural history, having been borne by numerous notable individuals from various walks of life. One of the most renowned historical figures with this name is the ancient Roman emperor Hadrian, who ruled from 117 to 138 AD. Known for his extensive travels throughout the Roman Empire and his building projects, such as Hadrian's Wall in Britain and the Pantheon in Rome, Hadrian left a lasting impact on Roman culture that is still felt today. In modern times, Adrien has been the given name of many celebrated artists, writers, and philosophers, showcasing the versatility and elegance of this name.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Adrien can be seen as a reminder of the inherent worth and importance of every individual. The Latin roots of Adrien, translating to 'man' or 'dark one', highlight the fundamental equality of all human beings, regardless of their background, appearance, or Station in life. This name can serve as a constant reminder for its bearers to embrace their unique identity and strive for personal growth, while demonstrating compassion towards others. Furthermore, Adrien can be seen as a connection to the themes of resilience and curiosity displayed by historical figures named Adrien, inspiring us to explore our own paths and face adversity with determination.
